question: In Figure 9E-12, what minimum distance separates the advance motor-vehicle stop line from the intersection stop line across the bicycle box?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The minimum separation is 10 feet. Figure 9E-12 annotates the dimension between the advance stop line (upstream edge of the bicycle box, where motor vehicles stop) and the intersection stop line (downstream edge of the box) as "10 ft MIN.," which reflects the mandatory Standard in Section 9E.12. Standards (mandatory): - "If used, the distance from the upstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest to the stop line for motor vehicles to the downstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest the crosswalk or intersection shall be at least 10 feet. At least one bicycle symbol marking (see Figure 9E-12) shall be used in the bicycle box." Options (permitted): - A bicycle box (see Figure 9E-12) may be used to increase the visibility of stopped bicycles on the approach to a signalized intersection during the red signal portion of the cycle for motor vehicles behind the box. - Green-colored pavement may be used in a bicycle box. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Drawing A of Figure 9E-12 (bicycle box across one lane) with the "Intersection stop line" and "Advance stop line" labeled and a "10 ft MIN." dimension between them; [Image 6] shows Sheet 2 of Figure 9E-12 (bicycle box across multiple lanes) with the same "10 ft MIN." dimension annotated on the northbound approach; [Image 5] confirms the same Sheet 1 layout in the full-page view with the 10 ft MIN. dimension. Citations: - Section 9E.12 Standard §6 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §1 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §12 (p.1106) - Figure 9E-12 (p.1106)
